text.p: Headlines from major national newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
EL PAIS
- Industry Minister Josep Pique appears ignorant about case brought against electricity firm Endesa by Spain's stock market commission.
EL MUNDO
- Signature of judge Baltasar Garzon on one of the "dirty war" documents published by El Pais this week proves that they were leaked from Defence Ministry.
- Mother and doctor advised cyclist Miguel Indurain to pull out of Banesto team.
DIARIO 16

- All deputies, apart from those from ruling Partido Popular, organised on Thursday a rebellion against Deputy Prime Minister Alvarez Cascos for his "inconsiderate and sexist attitude" in his controversial declarations about "women".
ABC
- Journalists Luis Maria Anson and Juan Luis Cebrian elected new members of Spain's Royal Academy.
CINCO DIAS
- BBV buys 40 percent stake in leading Venezuelan bank Provincial while Banco Santander buys 90 percent in second leading bank Banco de Venezuela.
- Construction firm Huarte lifts its suspension of payments.
- Company directors cannot treat themselves as independent with respect to Social Security.
EXPANSION
- Competition court opens case against electricity companies Iberdrola, Fenosa, Endesa and Unesa.
- French construction group Bouygues has sold 1.88 percent of BCH since July.
- Stock market posts another record high with general index breaking 420 barrier.
GACETA DE LOS NEGOCIOS
- Stock market commission's case against Endesa encourages removal of chairman Feliciano Fuster with possible replacements seen as Martin Villa, Juan Hoyos or Macia Alavedra.
- OCDE confirms Spain's recovery, but says it will not be enough to reduce unemployment.
